content: Women with severe liver disease, including those presenting with jaundice (a common sign of liver disease), are generally eligible to use combined oral contraceptives (COCs), levonorgestrel (LNG), or ulipristal acetate (UPA) for emergency contraception pills (ECPs), classified as Medical Eligibility Criteria (MEC) Category 2. Women taking medications that induce the CYP3A4 enzyme can use COCs, LNG, or UPA for ECPs without restrictions, classified as MEC Category 1. There are no restrictions on the repeated use of COCs, LNG, or UPA for ECPs, which are also classified as MEC Category 1. In cases of rape, there are no restrictions on the use of COCs, LNG, or UPA for ECPs, classified as MEC Category 1. Women at increased risk of sexually transmitted infections (STIs) can generally initiate the use of either copper-bearing intrauterine devices (Cu-IUDs) or levonorgestrel-releasing intrauterine devices (LNG-IUDs), classified as MEC Category 2. Similarly, women at increased risk of STIs can generally continue using Cu-IUDs or LNG-IUDs, also classified as MEC Category 2. Women at high risk of acquiring HIV can use all hormonal contraceptive methods, including COCs, combined injectable contraceptives (CICs), combined contraceptive patches and rings, progestogen-only pills (POPs), progestogen-only injectables (POIs) such as depot medroxyprogesterone acetate (DMPA) and norethisterone enanthate (NET-EN), and implants containing LNG or etonogestrel (ETG), without restrictions (MEC Category 1). LNG-IUDs can generally be used by these women, classified as MEC Category 2. Women living with asymptomatic or mild HIV clinical disease (WHO Stage 1 or 2) can use all hormonal contraceptive methods without restrictions (MEC Category 1). They can also generally use LNG-IUDs, classified as MEC Category 2. Women living with severe or advanced HIV clinical disease (WHO Stage 3 or 4) can use all hormonal contraceptive methods without restrictions (MEC Category 1). However, they are generally advised not to initiate LNG-IUD use (MEC Category 3) until their condition improves to asymptomatic or mild HIV clinical disease (WHO Stage 1 or 2). Women who already have an LNG-IUD inserted and later develop severe or advanced HIV do not need to have the IUD removed (MEC Category 2 for continuation). Women taking nucleoside/nucleotide reverse transcriptase inhibitors (NRTIs) as part of antiretroviral therapy (ART) can use all hormonal contraceptive methods without restrictions (MEC Category 1). They can also generally use LNG-IUDs (MEC Category 2) if their HIV clinical disease is asymptomatic or mild (WHO Stage 1 or 2). Women with severe or advanced HIV clinical disease (WHO Stage 3 or 4) taking NRTIs are generally advised not to initiate LNG-IUD use (MEC Category 3) until their condition improves. However, women already using LNG-IUDs who develop severe or advanced HIV do not need to have the IUD removed (MEC Category 2 for continuation). Women using non-nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitors (NNRTIs) containing efavirenz or nevirapine can generally use COCs, CICs, combined contraceptive patches and rings, POPs, NET-EN, and LNG or ETG implants (MEC Category 2). DMPA can be used without restrictions (MEC Category 1). LNG-IUDs can generally be used (MEC Category 2) if the HIV clinical disease is asymptomatic or mild (WHO Stage 1 or 2). Women with severe or advanced HIV clinical disease (WHO Stage 3 or 4) taking NNRTIs are generally advised not to initiate LNG-IUD use (MEC Category 3) until their condition improves. Women already using LNG-IUDs who develop severe or advanced HIV do not need to have the IUD removed (MEC Category 2 for continuation). Women using newer NNRTIs containing etravirine or rilpivirine can use all hormonal contraceptive methods without restrictions (MEC Category 1). Women taking protease inhibitors (PIs), including those boosted with ritonavir, can generally use COCs, CICs, combined contraceptive patches and rings, POPs, NET-EN, and LNG or ETG implants (MEC Category 2). DMPA can be used without restrictions (MEC Category 1). LNG-IUDs can generally be used (MEC Category 2) if the HIV clinical disease is asymptomatic or mild (WHO Stage 1 or 2). Women with severe or advanced HIV clinical disease (WHO Stage 3 or 4) taking PIs are generally advised not to initiate LNG-IUD use (MEC Category 3) until their condition improves. Women already using LNG-IUDs who develop severe or advanced HIV do not need to have the IUD removed (MEC Category 2 for continuation). Women using the integrase inhibitor raltegravir can use all hormonal contraceptive methods without restrictions (MEC Category 1). LNG-IUDs can generally be used (MEC Category 2) if the HIV clinical disease is asymptomatic or mild (WHO Stage 1 or 2). Women with severe or advanced HIV clinical disease (WHO Stage 3 or 4) taking raltegravir are generally advised not to initiate LNG-IUD use (MEC Category 3) until their condition improves. Women already using LNG-IUDs who develop severe or advanced HIV do not need to have the IUD removed (MEC Category 2 for continuation). The WHO guidelines aim to improve access to and quality of family planning services by providing evidence-based recommendations for policymakers, healthcare providers, and program managers. These recommendations are periodically updated to reflect advancements in medical and scientific knowledge.
